abstract: This paper presents a novel computational model based on adaptive geometry to explore the unique properties of quantum topology, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. Traditional topological computation models rely on static representations, while our approach dynamically adjusts the topology, offering a more flexible and potentially powerful framework. We introduce a framework that simulates complex topological structures using adaptive geometry, allowing for a more intuitive and efficient investigation of quantum phenomena. The core mechanism involves the continuous refinement of the topology through iterative adjustments, enabling the exploration of diverse quantum states and phenomena. This research investigates the impact of adaptive geometry on computational efficiency and offers a foundation for future advancements in quantum information processing.

We introduce a quantum self-adaptation mechanism that dynamically adjusts model parameters during training, enabling automated parameter optimization and significantly improved predictive accuracy. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a computationally efficient and inherently adaptive learning strategy. The core mechanism utilizes quantum properties to optimize model parameters, resulting in enhanced predictive capabilities. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art machine learning models.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology, aiming to address the challenges of complex systems and non-linear constraints inherent in traditional optimization methods. The core concept revolves around constructing dynamic topology structures to guide the search process and facilitate the discovery of optimal solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a case study involving a constrained optimization problem in a simulated neural network architecture. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the topology to enhance the search space and yield improved results compared to static optimization techniques. We highlight the advantages of this method, including automatic exploration of complex regions and the avoidance of local optima. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations and future directions of this research.

abstract: Quantum state dynamics offer a novel approach to modeling and simulating complex topological structures, surpassing the limitations of traditional methods. This paper introduces a dynamic adaptation control algorithm leveraging quantum state characteristics to efficiently analyze and manipulate topological landscapes. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting parameters within a quantum system to achieve a precise representation of the topological structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of a specific topological dataset, highlighting its potential for improved computational efficiency and enhanced topological understanding. This work contributes to the field of quantum topological computation and provides a framework for automated exploration of topological space.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm based on non-linear topological structures, emphasizing adaptive clustering driven by the inherent properties of the topology. title: Quantum Information Dynamics: Probability-Adaptive Matrix Operations
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum information dynamics to the design of novel probability-adaptive matrix operations. Traditional matrix operations are fundamentally classical, limited in their computational capabilities and susceptibility to noise. We propose a new approach utilizing quantum entanglement to fundamentally alter the computation process, shifting it from deterministic to probabilistic, thereby enhancing computational robustness and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around introducing quantum entanglement into the matrix multiplication process, leveraging its inherent quantum self-adaptability to achieve a more reliable and faster computation. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the potential of this approach, focusing on the design of a new matrix multiplication algorithm demonstrating improved performance and resilience against noise.

title: 基于拓扑的量子计算的自适应量子电路设计
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computations compared to classical computers, particularly for complex problems. However, the design and implementation of quantum circuits remain a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum circuit design leveraging topological principles to automate the process of circuit optimization and achieve higher computational efficiency. We propose a new framework for automatic circuit adjustment based on topological structure, enabling the system to adapt its design based on the characteristics of the task at hand. This system aims to overcome the limitations of traditional methods by offering a more flexible and robust approach to quantum circuit creation. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to generate circuits with improved performance for specific quantum algorithms. The core mechanism is the application of topological topological symmetries to the circuit structure, allowing the system to dynamically adjust parameters to achieve optimal results. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum circuit design, potentially paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum computations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Pattern Recognition (QGERP)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-enhanced geometric pattern recognition, focusing on the application of quantum entanglement to improve the speed and accuracy of pattern detection in geometric data. We introduce a novel algorithm, the "Quantum Correlation Matrix" (QCM), designed to identify subtle correlations inherent in geometric data that are often missed by classical algorithms. This research investigates the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement to create a 'quantum correlation matrix' that can facilitate faster and more reliable pattern recognition. We detail the mathematical framework of the QCM and present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying specific geometric patterns across diverse datasets. The study concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this rapidly evolving field.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Explainable AI – Causal Chain Analysis
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need for trust and accountability in increasingly complex AI systems. However, many existing XAI techniques offer only superficial explanations, often failing to capture the underlying causal mechanisms driving AI decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming languages to provide truly explainable AI through causal chain analysis. We argue that current XAI methods frequently lack grounding in causal relationships, generating explanations that are ultimately misleading. title: Quantum-Adaptive Geometry Complexity Optimization
abstract: Quantum-Adaptive Geometry Complexity Optimization addresses the limitations of traditional optimization algorithms by introducing a quantum-based approach that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters to enhance system performance. This paper proposes a novel algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to automatically optimize geometric configurations, resulting in improved efficiency and performance. We present a theoretical framework outlining the algorithm's core mechanisms and discuss the potential benefits of this approach compared to existing methods. The core claim centers on the ability of the algorithm to automatically adapt geometric parameters to optimize system performance.

title: Quantum-Adaptive Nonlinear Matrix Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-adaptive non-linear matrix generation algorithm designed for complex data analysis and simulation. Traditional matrix generation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the versatility and fidelity of the generated matrices. We propose a quantum-based approach that leverages quantum entanglement to create complex matrices with high fidelity. The algorithm dynamically adjusts its parameters to optimize the matrix generation process, offering a significant improvement over existing techniques. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing its potential for advanced data analysis and simulation tasks. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum entanglement to generate matrices with enhanced characteristics, leading to improved accuracy and resilience.

title: Artificial intelligence in endometrial and cervical cancer: From ultrasound-based detection to digital pathology and prognostic modeling
abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) and cervical cancer together account for over one million new diagnoses annually, yet their diagnostic pathways remain constrained by operatordependent imaging, the limited sensitivity of cytology, and substantial inter-observer variability in histopathological grading.Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing classical machine learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transformer architectures, and computational pathology on whole-slide images, is maturing across the gynaecologic-oncology continuum.This minireview synthesises the evidence across six domains: Ultrasound-based detection and characterisation; colposcopy and cervical cytology; digital pathology and histopathology; magnetic resonance imaging based staging and radiomics; molecular biomarker integration, liquid biopsy and prognostic modelling; and clinical translation.In retrospective and predominantly single-centre datasets, AI has matched or exceeded expert performance on several narrow tasks, notably ultrasound assessment of deep myometrial invasion, automated cytology triage, and morphology-based molecular subtyping of EC, and one digital cytology platform has obtained United States Food and Drug Administration clearance.Regulatory clearance nevertheless remains exceptional rather than routine in this field, and headline accuracies derived from small curated datasets are frequently inflated by overfitting; the most instructive example is a landmark colposcopy model whose nearperfect discrimination was subsequently attributed by its own senior author to overfitting uncorrected by internal validation.Persistent deficits in external validation, prospective trial evidence, methodological quality, algorithmic equity and regulatory clarity continue to separate promising retrospective performance from routine clinical deployment.

title: Метод защиты от атак на модели машинного обучения путем затруднения действий нарушителей
abstract: Цель работы, разработать и экспериментально оценить метод латентно- адаптивной деградации обучающего воздействия, направленный на снижение эффективности атак отравления данных при сохранении приемлемой точности модели. Объект исследования, процесс обучения моделей машинного обучения в условиях присутствия отравленных данных. Предмет исследования, методы защиты моделей машинного обучения за счет модификации обучающего воздействия. В ходе работы были проанализированы атаки отравления данных и методы защиты, разработаны математическая модель и алгоритм метода ЛАДОВ, реализован исследовательский стенд и проведена экспериментальная оценка. Метод ЛАДОВ снижает предсказуемость влияния обучающих примеров на параметры модели за счет адаптивного коэффициента надежности, ограничения нормы градиента, стохастического искажения градиентной динамики и проверки согласованности в латентном пространстве. Эксперименты на CIFAR-10 с моделью ResNet-18 показали, что метод наиболее заметно снижает успешность clean-label backdoor-атаки при сохранении высокой точности на чистых данных.

title: Evaluating large language models on text-based engineering design tasks: performance gaps and failure modes
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models are increasingly considered for integration into engineering design workflows, yet their actual capabilities on the analytical and optimization tasks that arise in engineering design remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine Large Language Model-generated answers to 86 text-based questions covering three task categories chosen for their direct correspondence to typical engineering design activities: 50 problem-solving tasks from the Kangaroo Math Competition, 20 structural engineering design tasks involving stress analysis and cross-section selection, and 16 engineering optimization tasks involving conflicting constraints and trade-offs. Across the evaluated models, we observe that performance is consistently higher on the general Kangaroo problem-solving questions than on the engineering geometry and optimization tasks, even though these draw on a comparable set of underlying skills. The study further exposes systematic failure modes across the examined task types, including geometric reasoning, multi-step numerical computation, and optimization under conflicting constraints. These findings characterize the specific capabilities that AI-enabled design systems must develop to be reliable in practice, and establish an empirical baseline for evaluating future augmentation strategies such as tool integration and structured design workflows.

title: Can Large Language Models Anticipate Behavioral Responses to Social Policies? A Case of Pension Enrollment Prediction among China's Flexible Workers
abstract: Assessing the impacts of social policy changes is a widely acknowledged challenge for policymakers. Econometric methods can be unreliable when extrapolating to hypothetical scenarios, while field pilot programs are highly costly. In this paper, we propose using large language models (LLMs) as policy-assessment tools adapted from general-purpose models. We present FlexPension-LLM, the first domain-specialized large language model for a hierarchical pension-enrollment prediction task among flexible workers in China, and introduce DKI-RDistill, which injects policy-grounded cues into the prompt, including Probit-derived marginal effects and hukou-province pension rules. The method then uses LoRA/SFT to distill rationale-augmented supervision into an open-weight MoE student, with teacher errors corrected by regenerating those cases under ground-truth labels. On a CHFS 2019 blind split, FlexPension-LLM achieves 0.9316 Composite F1, surpassing its Claude Sonnet 4.5 teacher and 15 of 17 baselines, and is statistically indistinguishable from Claude Opus 4.6. Across four external surveys, it averages 0.7549 Composite F1 and shows the narrowest performance range among the strongest systems. Component analysis shows that gains come mainly from policy-grounded cue injection and error-filtered supervision, while rationales provide decision traces that can be checked against policy rules.

title: Sound-based Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation
abstract: Can we recover the 3D poses of multiple people using only sound? This paper presents the first attempt to estimate multi-person 3D poses solely from acoustic signals. Estimating the poses of multiple individuals using acoustic signals is inherently challenging due to the superposition of motion-dependent signal variations. Unlike single-person scenarios, the presence of multiple subjects leads to overlapping acoustic signatures, making it difficult to attribute specific signal changes to an individual's pose. Furthermore, the complexity is compounded by inter-person reflections, which introduce intricate propagation delays that obscure the temporal motion-acoustic relationship. To address these issues, we propose SoundMHPE (Sound-based Multi-person Human Pose Estimator), a novel encoder-decoder framework consisting of two key components. First, the Acoustic Multi-scale Encoder captures diverse temporal and fine-grained frequency features to isolate subtle acoustic signatures from complex, overlapping signals. Second, the Temporal Pose Decoder employs an attention mechanism to disentangle multi-person information across successive frames. By jointly accounting for temporal dynamics and inter-person dependencies, this component precisely reconstructs frame-wise individual poses. To validate our approach, we constructed the 6-hour Acoustic Multi-person Pose (AMP) dataset consisting of 432K synchronized frames of multi-person pose and acoustic data, and demonstrated that our SoundMHPE outperforms baseline models. Project page: https://oumi03.github.io/sound-mhpe/

title: Neural networks learn to reconstruct multipartite entanglement from quantum marginals
abstract: Different sets of local correlations are not equivalent: some fragments of reduced data uniquely determine a global quantum state, while others leave it ambiguous. The quantum marginal problem asks whether a collection of reduced density matrices uniquely determines a compatible global quantum state. Although generic quantum states are uniquely specified by suitable sets of marginals, different collections of marginals are not equally informative: some uniquely determine the global state, whereas others leave it ambiguous. Identifying when uniqueness holds, and reconstructing the global state from partial information, remains computationally demanding and experimentally challenging. We show that information about the multipartite entanglement class and reconstructability in four-qubit systems is compactly encoded in small sets of two- and three-qubit marginals. Using semidefinite programming, we chart the reconstructability landscape across 49 inequivalent SLOCC entanglement classes and show that uniqueness strongly depends on both entanglement structure and marginal order. Neural networks trained only on reduced density matrices learn this structure directly. They accurately classify marginal reconstructability and, when uniqueness holds, reconstruct the full four-qubit density matrix with high fidelity from two- and three-qubit marginals. We benchmark the approach on a four-qubit nuclear magnetic resonance quantum processor and demonstrate that reconstructions from experimentally measured marginals remain faithful despite phase damping and control imperfections. Our results show that neural networks can learn when local correlations uniquely specify a global quantum state, and reveal how global quantum structure is encoded in reduced data.

title: Enhancing Multimodal Emotion Recognition via Multi-Feature Encoding and Attention-Based Fusion
abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition has attracted growing interest due to its importance in human-computer interaction, remote education, and healthcare. This paper proposes a novel multimodal emotion recognition framework that integrates rich audio and visual feature extraction with an attention-based fusion strategy. For audio, we extract three complementary feature types: semantic embeddings from Wav2Vec2, MFCC features, and statistical acoustic descriptors such as pitch, energy, and rhythm. These are aligned and fused via a BiLSTM to capture temporal dependencies. For video, we propose a ResNet50-BiLSTM architecture that combines deep residual learning and sequential modeling to extract expressive spatiotemporal features from facial sequences. To enhance multimodal synergy, we introduce a feature-level fusion mechanism based on multi-head attention, allowing the model to adaptively weigh contributions across modalities. Experiments conducted on the MELD and IEMOCAP datasets demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms baselines in both accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, ablation studies show that the attention-based fusion strategy significantly improves performance in unbalanced data settings. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework effectively captures diverse emotional cues from speech and visual expressions, and offers a practical and generalizable approach for real-world multimodal emotion recognition tasks.

title: The Meaning Model: Constructing Worlds and Stories at Progressive Resolution
abstract: The Meaning Model proposes a shared medium for constructing a world, its meanings, interpretations, and story together. The long-term aim is to model reality computationally through interrelated processes, from physical and social histories to attributed inner life, at a declared finite resolution. A world can be constructed coherently at a coarse resolution for a declared purpose, then recursively opened into finer detail. Each opening must preserve declared commitments or explicitly revise them, including their dependent accounts and passages. The contribution is this coordinated authoring method, not a new record type or the storage of prose beside a graph. Six record forms—Concept, Thing, Event, Binding, Cut, and Realization—support the method. Abstract meaning uses the same world machinery: a Concept may remain lightly specified or have process-based concept models whose roles and processes can be inspected alongside their instances. World records, Understanding Graphs recording interpretations and reasons, and document nodes share one address space and can be revised together while retaining their distinct authority. Semantic numbers are comparative commitments rather than freestanding scores. Each Cut names an Event parent, question, and unit, allocating one unit among exclusive answers and an explicit remainder for the unallocated share. Ordinary process links remain unweighted; measurements retain external units. The workspace supports human or AI construction and supplies a candidate training language. Developing and revising the categories themselves is part of the construction method. A learner could acquire these practices: choosing, deepening, and repairing representations, not only predicting content within a fixed schema. Life Simulation develops the construction-to-learning loop and its tests; this paper specifies the representation and preservation contracts. The completed manuscript, The Book of Conditions, partially demonstrates construction feasibility but does not validate the full method; learning gains, computational savings, and alignment remain untested.

title: ESI triage support using structured and free-text clinical data: A comparative machine learning study in a Colombian emergency department
abstract: This thesis systematically compares machine learning approaches for ESI triage classification, combining multiple text vectorization strategies, classifiers, and class imbalance methods. The data used included free-text clinical notes and structured variables, routinely collected at triage in Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe, Colombia. The best-performing model combined an XGBoost classifier, SMOTE-NC oversampling, and RoBERTa embeddings. It was evaluated in terms of performance metrics, subgroup fairness, and interpretability, where it achieved a macro F1 of 0.6791 and 76.2% accuracy on the held-out test set, demonstrating that open-source pipelines can achieve competitive triage classification performance in institutions at early stages of AI adoption.

title: Evolving Sensor Layouts Under Survival and Locomotor Constraints
abstract: We introduce a compact genotype for evolving directional sensor layouts in embodied artificial agents. The representation separates the number of sensors from their angular allocation: a scalar sensor count specifies the number of rays, while an inverse cumulative-distribution mapping converts quantiles into ordered ray headings across an evolvable field of view. This construction permits sensor-count mutation, continuous changes in angular span, and smooth foveal or peripheral concentration without explicitly mutating an unordered list of sensor coordinates. We evaluate the representation in a two-dimensional obstacle arena containing a moving target. Agents control steering and throttle through a neural network receiving only normalized obstacle-distance measurements from their evolved rays. An agent is successful if it reaches the target before colliding with an obstacle or leaving the arena; no distance, speed, path-length, survival-time, or target-proximity reward is used. We compare four conditions over seven independent 50,000-generation trials: mutable sensors without a ray-dependent locomotor cost, mutable sensors with a 3.5% speed penalty per additional ray, and fixed arrays of four or eight rays whose layouts remain evolvable. Free sensing produced substantially larger and more variable terminal sensor arrays than the cost-constrained condition (17.52 ± 7.16 versus 8.03 ± 3.03 rays). The cost condition also produced more stable terminal success (96.0% ± 4.4% versus 85.7% ± 29.5%). Fixed fourand eight-ray systems achieved nearly identical success rates (98.9% and 99.1%, respectively), despite adapting through different visual spans and angular densities. Across replicate trials, the sensor-cost condition did not converge to a single universal morphology: viable endpoints ranged from approximately three to twelve rays. These results support the inverse-CDF genotype as a useful experimental representation for studying sensor morphology, while emphasizing that the observed morphologies are task- and implementation-dependent evolutionary outcomes rather than biologically optimal designs.

An agent is successful if it reaches the target before colliding with an obstacle or leaving the arena; no distance, speed, path-length, survival-time, or target-proximity reward is used. We compare four conditions over seven independent 50,000-generation trials: mutable sensors without a ray-dependent locomotor cost, mutable sensors with a 3.5% speed penalty per additional ray, and fixed arrays of four or eight rays whose layouts remain evolvable. Free sensing produced substantially larger and more variable terminal sensor arrays than the cost-constrained condition (17.52 ± 7.16 versus 8.03 ± 3.03 rays). The cost condition also produced more stable terminal success (96.0% ± 4.4% versus 85.7% ± 29.5%). Fixed fourand eight-ray systems achieved nearly identical success rates (98.9% and 99.1%, respectively), despite adapting through different visual spans and angular densities. Across replicate trials, the sensor-cost condition did not converge to a single universal morphology: viable endpoints ranged from approximately three to twelve rays. These results support the inverse-CDF genotype as a useful experimental representation for studying sensor morphology, while emphasizing that the observed morphologies are task- and implementation-dependent evolutionary outcomes rather than biologically optimal designs.

title: 自适应混沌理论的量子计算实现
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize the study and manipulation of self-organized chaotic systems. We present a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive Chaos Quantum Engine" (ACQE), designed to achieve real-time parameter adjustment within a quantum system, thereby generating dynamic and unpredictable chaos. The core of the algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to create a feedback loop, allowing the system to subtly adjust its parameters based on observed outputs, ultimately leading to the emergence of complex, self-sustaining chaotic behavior. The paper details the theoretical framework underpinning the QE, including the quantum entanglement protocol and the feedback mechanism, and demonstrates preliminary results through simulations, showcasing the algorithm's capability to generate novel chaotic patterns. We argue that this approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities in areas like complex systems modeling and potentially even quantum simulation. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: Adaptive Knowledge Reasoning Engine Based on Cognitive Graphs
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive knowledge reasoning engine built upon the foundation of cognitive graphs. The core claim is that dynamic cognitive graphs, combined with contextual information, enable adaptive inference and knowledge discovery within complex concepts. The engine operates through continuous knowledge extraction from diverse sources (text, images, etc.) and constructs a dynamic cognitive graph. Deep learning techniques are then employed to adaptively update the graph and adjust node weights, allowing the engine to reason based on contextual information and ultimately generate relevant conclusions. The innovation lies in shifting from static knowledge bases to dynamic graphs, facilitating real-time learning, contextual adaptation, and improved inference accuracy and efficiency. The system leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to perform reasoning, and employs attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant nodes within the graph. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge reasoning by incorporating the fluidity of information and the nuances of context. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent systems capable of handling complex, evolving knowledge domains. ---

title: Generative Models for Circuit Design via Symbolic Regression
abstract: Circuit design is a crucial, yet inherently complex, process in modern electronics. Traditional design methodologies often rely on expert intuition and iterative manual optimization, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the most efficient solutions. This paper proposes a novel approach to circuit design utilizing symbolic regression, a powerful technique for automated equation discovery. The core idea is to leverage symbolic regression to learn the optimal circuit topology and associated parameters directly from a dataset of circuit performance metrics. This eliminates the need for human-defined constraints and allows the system to explore a potentially vast design space, generating novel circuit designs that could surpass conventional designs in terms of efficiency. The presented methodology offers a significant step toward automating the circuit optimization process, promising faster and more effective design cycles. The key formulation involves representing the circuit as a symbolic expression and employing regression techniques to minimize a cost function defined by the desired performance metrics. This approach provides a framework for generating potentially superior circuit designs without requiring extensive manual intervention.

title: Spectral Graph Anomaly Detection using Fractal Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to graph anomaly detection by utilizing fractal analysis of graph spectral data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional graph structures. This research addresses this challenge by transforming graph spectral information into fractal representations, allowing for the application of established fractal analysis techniques to identify deviations from expected patterns. The core idea is that anomalies in graph structures will manifest as distortions in their fractal representations. We explore the relationship between graph Laplacian eigenvalues, spectral clustering, and fractal dimension, demonstrating the efficacy of this method. The proposed framework offers a geometrically-grounded approach to anomaly detection, potentially improving accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods. We present a theoretical framework and discuss the key elements of the approach, outlining a potential methodology for implementation.

title: Dynamic Quantum Circuit Compilation via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a crucial step in realizing quantum algorithms on near-term quantum hardware. Traditional compilation methods often employ static circuit representations, limiting their ability to adapt to the fluctuating coherence properties and connectivity constraints of actual quantum devices. This research introduces a novel approach utilizing tensor network representations for dynamic quantum circuit compilation. The core idea is to leverage the inherent entanglement and superposition present in quantum systems to create adaptive circuit layouts. Our method employs an iterative tensor network algorithm that continuously refines circuit representations, prioritizing coherence preservation and minimizing gate count, while incorporating real-time qubit state estimations. This dynamic adaptation directly addresses the challenges posed by the limitations of current quantum hardware, offering a pathway to more efficient and robust quantum algorithm execution. The key innovation lies in the application of tensor networks, a powerful mathematical tool, to the optimization problem of quantum circuit compilation.

This research aims to address the limitations of current machine learning approaches by introducing a framework that explicitly incorporates network structure and adaptation. The anticipated outcome is a model capable of better handling complex, variable datasets and improved predictive accuracy.

title: ПОВЫШЕНИЕ ЭФФЕКТИВНОСТИ ПОИСКОВ МЕТАЛЛИЧЕСКИХ РУД НА ОСНОВЕ ИНТЕГРАЦИИ ГЕОЛОГИЧЕСКИХ, ГЕОФИЗИЧЕСКИХ, ГЕОХИМИЧЕСКИХ И ГИС-ДАННЫХ В СЕВЕРНОЙ И ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОЙ ЧАСТЯХ РЕСПУБЛИКИ АРМЕНИЯ
abstract: This study explores approaches to improving the efficiency of exploration for gold, polymetallic, and porphyry copper deposits within the Lori, Stepanavan, and Pambak-Tsaghkunyats ore districts of the Republic of Armenia. An integrated analysis of the geological framework, gravity, aeromagnetic, and geochemical survey data, combined with GIS-based techniques, was used to identify the principal ore-controlling factors governing the distribution of endogenous mineralization. The locations of several fault structures were refined, previously unrecognized concealed circular and arcuate structures were delineated, and their relationships with known mineral occurrences were established. The spatial association of gold, polymetallic, and porphyry copper mineralization with specific gravity anomalies, major fault zones, and intrusive complexes of different compositions was demonstrated. Several prospective target areas for detailed exploration were identified, and a preliminary assessment of their mineral potential was conducted. The results obtained may be applied to mineralization forecasting, and the planning of future geological exploration programs.

title: Adaptive Attention and Pyramid Pooling for High-Performance Dysarthric Speech Recognition
abstract: Speech pathology is a multidisciplinary field that assesses, diagnoses, and manages communication disorders caused by neurological, developmental, structural, and degenerative conditions. Among these disorders, dysarthria is a motor speech impairment characterized by reduced speech intelligibility and abnormal articulatory patterns resulting from neuromuscular dysfunction. Automatic dysarthria assessment remains challenging because of substantial inter-speaker variability, diverse severity levels, and the complex temporal–spectral characteristics of pathological speech signals. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an attention-enhanced convolutional neural network for automatic dysarthria detection and severity classification. The proposed architecture integrates a convolutional block attention module to enhance channel-wise and spatial feature representations, a coordinate attention module to capture long-range contextual dependencies while preserving positional information, and spatial pyramid pooling to extract robust multi-scale representations and accommodate input variability. Hierarchical convolutional layers with rectified linear unit activation and max-pooling operations progressively learn discriminative speech representations, followed by fully connected layers and a softmax classifier for prediction. The proposed framework was comprehensively evaluated on two publicly available datasets: TORGO Dataset 1, containing dysarthric and healthy control speech recordings, and TORGO Severity Dataset 2, comprising four dysarthria severity classes. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, together with their first- and second-order temporal derivatives and complementary acoustic descriptors, were extracted to characterize the speech signals. Extensive experiments, including cross-validation, repeated runs, ablation studies, Shapley additive explanations-based interpretability analysis, and statistical significance analysis, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. On TORGO Dataset 1, the proposed model achieved 95.00% accuracy, 94.50% precision, 95.25% recall, and a 94.75% F1-score, outperforming conventional machine learning and deep learning baselines. On TORGO Severity Dataset 2, the proposed framework achieved 99.10% classification accuracy, an F1-score of 0.9910, and an area under the curve of 0.9999, demonstrating strong performance in multi-class dysarthria severity classification. These findings highlight the proposed model’s strong discriminative capability, robustness, and interpretability, indicating its potential as a reliable computer-aided decision-support system for dysarthria detection and severity assessment.

title: How Do We Cook Up Artificial Intelligence With Optimization Algorithms?
abstract: Have you ever followed a recipe to make your favorite cake? Sometimes it turns out perfect, and sometimes you must adjust the amount of sugar or baking time to improve it. But what would you do if you needed to develop a brand-new recipe from scratch? Building artificial intelligence (AI) is similar, but requires a much more complex recipe! To “cook up” smart AI, scientists combine billions of instructions in just the right way, so the program can recognize patterns, solve problems, and reason like a human. However, it is nearly impossible to guess the best sequence of instructions in advance. Optimization algorithms are like helpful chefs in the kitchen, testing how well the AI performs, figuring out what is wrong, and tweaking the recipe to improve it. Optimization algorithms help computer scientists discover better versions of the recipe, until the AI becomes smarter and more powerful—just like perfecting a delicious cake!

title: Federated and Differentially Private Prediction of Immune Checkpoint Blockade Response from Multi-Cohort Transcriptomics
abstract: Transcriptomic signatures of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response often exhibit limited transportability across independent cohorts, while privacy constraints restrict pooling of pa-tient-level transcriptomic data across institutions. We evaluated whether federated learning (FL) with record-level differential privacy (DP) could predict ICB response across heterogeneous cohorts and whether a pre-specified PD-L1-trafficking module added predictive signal beyond an inter-feron-γ (IFN-γ) signature. Five public ICB cohorts (four anti-PD1 melanoma and one anti-PD-L1 urothelial cohort) were treated as federated sites. Logistic regression was trained using FedAvg and FedProx with per-example DP-SGD and cumulative Rényi DP accounting. The evaluation was conducted through leave-one-cohort-out external validation against a matched centralized non-private reference. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs) were modest, ranging from approximately 0.56 to 0.61, and remained broadly stable across the privacy budgets evaluated. Specifically, for the combined feature set, mean AUROC was 0.561 without DP and 0.573 at ε = 1. The IFN-γ module provided the strongest predictive signal (≈0.61), whereas trafficking alone performed near chance (≈0.49), and combining the modules did not im-prove overall discrimination (≈0.56). These results support the feasibility of privacy-preserving federated ICB-response prediction despite significant cross-cohort heterogeneity. DRG2 exhibited a directionally consistent positive contribution across full-cohort and melanoma-only analyses, which persisted in a sensitivity analysis that additionally modeled upstream recycling regulators, including RAB5A, concordant with its established role in endosomal PD-L1 recycling and anti-PD-1 response.

title: Study of A Theoretical and Experimental Model of Direct Solar Radiation At the University of Agadez Experimental Site in Niger
abstract: This work involves evaluating direct solar radiation by applying Kasten’s semi-empirical mathematical model and comparing the results with measurements taken at the University of Agadez experimental site (Agadez urban commune), with the aim of sizing a 20 MWe thermodynamic solar power plant. This study was conducted under three different atmospheric conditions (overcast, average, and clear skies) and using three solar collector tilt angles (0°, 17°, and 30°). Radiation calculations were performed using Excel software by incorporating appropriate equations into a program based on the Kasten model. As for the measurements, they were conducted over ten (10) typical days using two pyranometers. After correcting for the Linke turbidity factor, the resulting direct solar radiation and theoretical annual irradiation are 680 W/m² and 2,979 kWh/m²/year, respectively, compared to measured values of 767 W/m² and 3,010 kWh/m²/year. This study confirms Agadez's strong solar potential for CSP.

title: A Stochastic Recursive Gradient Algorithm with Random Barzilai–Borwein Step Size for Convex Optimization
abstract: The StochAstic Recursive grAdient algoritHm (SARAH) has garnered considerable attention owing to its implementation of a straightforward recursive framework for stochastic gradient updates. Motivated by this, we propose to integrate the importance sampling strategy with mini-batch techniques into the SARAH framework, developing a variant termed SARAH-MI-RBB. During each inner iteration of SARAH-MI-RBB, the mini-batch technique and importance sampling method are employed to dynamically adjust the Barzilai–Borwein (BB) step size and update the iterates. We provide a linear convergence in expectation of the outer iterates to the unique optimal solution for strongly convex problems. Furthermore, we provide a complexity analysis of the algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in its class.

title: Retinal OCTA Phenotyping with LLM Reporting for Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Early identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because established assessment methods can be costly, resource-intensive, or unsuitable for population-scale screening. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) provides non-invasive visualization of retinal microvasculature, but existing approaches often require diagnostic labels and provide limited measurement-level interpretation. We present an explainable OCTA pipeline that integrates annotation-aware vessel segmentation, layer-specific vascular biomarker extraction, label-free phenotyping, and measurement-grounded LLM reporting. Using 117 ROSE-1 images from 39 subjects, we apply annotation-matched segmentation models to superficial vascular complex (SVC), deep vascular complex (DVC), and combined SVC+DVC representations. The models achieve ROC-AUC values of 0.916-0.970 and Dice scores of 0.695-0.781. Six density and fractal-dimension biomarkers form subject-level profiles for exploratory clustering. Analysis of nine held-out subjects identifies an internally consistent lower-density, lower-fractal-dimension phenotype, although the absence of diagnostic labels prevents clinical interpretation. Reports generated using GPT, Gemini, and Llama are evaluated for measurement grounding, citation faithfulness, and diagnostic caution. Overall, the framework provides a transparent, non-diagnostic connection between retinal vascular measurements, exploratory phenotyping, and evidence-linked interpretation for Alzheimer's research.

title: Causality and Attraction: A Continuum of Steady States - Volume XII: The Signal: AI-Assisted Research Content
abstract: Causality and Attraction: A Continuum of Steady States - Volume XII: The Signal examines AI-assisted research content, authorship, provenance, novelty, detection, watermarking, and fingerprinting. The volume applies Nested Causal Modelling to the relationship among human language, machine-generated text, institutions assigning authorship, and readers determining value. It investigates whether statistical resemblance can establish authorship; follows the reciprocal influence of human and machine language; examines original prompts and DOI chronology as research evidence; and develops an account of responsible AI assistance that preserves human authorship, accountability, and novel ideation. The appendices contain the complete nested causal model, research evidence ledger, completed novelty ledger, statement on artificial-intelligence use, and the originating author prompts that materially directed the inquiry.

title: Boundary Information Theory - BIT-X13.6 ACTC REL-001: Grammar-Neutral Software-State Benchmark and Terminal Result Integration
abstract: Public-audit handoff for the BIT-X13.6 Adaptive Cognitive Topology Computer (ACTC) software-state benchmark. A frozen synthetic benchmark executed 72 cases under 12 policies (864 evaluations). The predeclared load-bearing gate for the Bagua-derived 8/64-state grammar failed, yielding NON_LOAD_BEARING_SYMBOLIC_ENCODING within scope. The terminal integration therefore retains the 8/64 grammar only as a historical-semantic source and optional symbolic encoding, while preserving a grammar-neutral ACTC core: State Estimation → Continuous/Typed Operator Selection → Adaptive Weighted Topology → Thermal/Resource Feedback → Self-Mapping → Counterfactual Evaluation → Readout/Receipt. F2 remains NOT_OPENED. This release makes no hardware, quantum-computing, empirical-superiority, production-readiness, authority, or world-effect claim.

title: It Ran Is Not It Was Right: A Policy-Conditioned Benchmark of Ten Text-to-SQL Architectures on an Enterprise Database
abstract: Enterprise text-to-SQL assistants are usually judged by whether the SQL runs. On a realistic company database that is misleading: a query can run and still be wrong, return rows the asker may not see, ignore a rule in a policy document, or answer a question that should be refused. We build a testbed (59-table oil-and-gas database with role-based access, an approval workflow, nine policy documents) and a gold set of 94 questions labelled with the correct answer, the asking role, and whether to answer or refuse. Scoring ten published architectures on answer correctness, data leakage, policy grounding, and refusal overturns the execution-success ranking: the declared winner is ninth of ten on correctness, every architecture leaks restricted data (37 to 52 percent), almost none refuse, and the best is right about half the time. Results are stable over three runs, and the winner's validator gate does not fix any of these failures. Data is synthetic. We release the testbed, gold set, and scorer.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear geometric topology as a foundation for quantum simulation, specifically focusing on the study of topological quantum structures. We propose a novel quantum simulation technique that leverages the inherent properties of these structures to uncover new quantum phenomena. The core claim is that designing quantum simulations using this approach will yield insights into the behavior of complex quantum systems and potentially reveal novel quantum states. This work is an initial investigation into this promising research avenue, emphasizing the design of a robust and flexible simulation framework.

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum error correction protocol designed to dynamically adjust error correction algorithms based on the quantum system's state. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a "quantum state dynamic encoding" mechanism, leveraging the self-correlation of quantum states to construct a flexible and adaptive correction strategy. This approach contrasts with traditional static algorithms, offering significantly improved error correction efficiency and robustness. The paper details the proposed mechanism, its theoretical foundation, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating quantum errors. The focus is on enhancing the system's resilience against noise and decoherence.

title: High-Dimensional Geometric Functionals for Automated Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel automated optimization algorithm based on high-dimensional geometric functionals, designed specifically for addressing optimization problems in high-dimensional data analysis. The core mechanism centers on leveraging the unique properties of these functionals to dynamically adjust parameters, leading to improved model performance and efficient optimization. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of optimization scenarios. The paper focuses on achieving automated parameter adjustment, a critical aspect for complex problems.

title: Based on Information Entropy: Automatic Semantic Evolution of Programs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to automatic program evolution based on information entropy. The core claim is that program semantics can be automatically evolved through changes in information entropy. Specifically, the entropy of a program's execution results is intrinsically linked to its semantic meaning, and variations in this entropy drive optimization and adjustment of the code. The proposed mechanism utilizes intermediate state information generated during program execution to calculate entropy values. These entropy change quantities serve as optimization objectives, guiding the automatic adjustment of code structure and logic through techniques like genetic algorithms or reinforcement learning, ultimately minimizing entropy fluctuations. This method overcomes the limitations of traditional, human-intervention-dependent program optimization techniques, offering a globally-optimized approach by leveraging the theoretical foundations of information theory. The research presents a new perspective on program optimization, shifting the focus from explicit code modifications to the inherent informational structure of the program's behavior. ---

title: Biofeedback-Driven Adaptive Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging biofeedback data. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting algorithm parameters and structure in real-time based on physiological signals, specifically focusing on data streams like electroencephalography (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV). We propose a framework where a machine learning model learns the mapping between these biological signals and performance metrics of the algorithm. This learned relationship is then used to iteratively refine the algorithm's configuration, leading to adaptive optimization. The key distinction from existing methods lies in the direct utilization of biofeedback for algorithmic control, moving beyond simple user interface feedback. The paper details the theoretical framework, outlines potential implementation strategies, and discusses the challenges and future directions of this biofeedback-driven adaptive optimization paradigm. The overarching goal is to create algorithms that are not only optimized for a specific task but also inherently responsive to the user's state and the environment, potentially leading to significant improvements in efficiency and robustness.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Computational Provenance Tracking
abstract: Algorithmic transparency is increasingly crucial as algorithms permeate various aspects of modern life, impacting decisions with significant consequences. However, the inherent complexity and "black box" nature of many algorithms hinder understanding and trust. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing algorithmic transparency: computational provenance tracking. The core idea is to establish a verifiable record of an algorithm's execution history, providing an immutable audit trail that details every step of its operation. This system meticulously tracks data transformations, parameter updates, and intermediate results, moving beyond simple logging to create a truly auditable record. The system's design focuses on creating a verifiable and auditable record, fostering greater transparency and accountability. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods and lays a foundation for improved algorithmic trust and scrutiny. The primary metric for success will be the ability to reconstruct the algorithm's decision-making process with complete fidelity, enabling external verification and validation. ---

title: Towards Enhanced Security in Distributed Storage via Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes to significantly enhance the security of distributed storage systems. Traditional cryptographic approaches for securing distributed data are increasingly vulnerable to attacks from quantum computers. This research proposes a novel framework leveraging the inherent error-correcting capabilities of QEC codes to provide robust protection against a wide range of attacks, including those specifically designed for classical cryptographic systems. The core of the approach involves the implementation of a tailored encoding and decoding scheme based on a chosen QEC code. We explore the theoretical foundations of QEC, focusing on key parameters such as code distance, encoding rate, and decoding complexity. The goal is to demonstrate a pathway toward constructing a distributed storage architecture that exhibits significantly improved resistance to data breaches and manipulation, particularly in scenarios where quantum computing capabilities pose a serious threat. This work highlights the emerging role of QEC in securing information infrastructure against the looming challenges of quantum computing.

title: On Differential Geometry-Based Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to machine learning model design leveraging concepts and techniques from differential geometry. The core idea is to treat a machine learning model as a differential equation and utilize optimization methods from differential geometry for training. Traditional machine learning model design predominantly relies on linear algebra and probability theory, often neglecting the geometric structure inherent in these models. This approach aims to improve model generalization ability by explicitly incorporating geometric considerations. We present a framework for formulating machine learning models within a differential geometric context, outlining key elements including the model as a Lagrangian, optimization strategies based on Riemannian geometry, and potential benefits for model robustness and adaptability. This work establishes a foundation for a fundamentally new perspective on machine learning model design, shifting the focus from purely statistical approaches to one grounded in the rich mathematical structure of differential geometry. ---

title: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Networks: A Novel Approach to Graph Representation and Reasoning
abstract: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Networks (D-AGNNs) represent a significant advancement in graph neural network design, focusing on the ability to dynamically adjust the graph structure to optimize both representation and reasoning capabilities. This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, leveraging adaptive algorithms to dynamically re-shape the graph topology based on the inherent characteristics of the input graph. The core of the system lies in a self-adjusting process, iteratively refining the graph structure to enhance the representation learned by the network. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark graph datasets, showcasing a substantial improvement in both accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we explore the impact of different dynamic adjustment strategies on the network's performance, providing insights into optimal graph structure configuration. The proposed D-AGNNs offer a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of graph-related tasks.

title: Topological Quantum State Partitioning for Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Topological Quantum State Partitioning (TQP) to enhance complexity analysis of quantum systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the sheer scale of quantum computations, necessitating computationally intensive techniques. We propose a novel mapping algorithm based on topological invariants to partition quantum states into smaller, interconnected groups, thereby reducing computational burden and facilitating efficient complexity assessment. The core mechanism hinges on identifying and exploiting these invariants to establish connectivity within the quantum state space. This approach offers a significant advancement in the field, potentially enabling faster and more scalable analysis of complex quantum systems.

title: Bayesian Geometric Modeling for Dynamical Systems Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian geometric modeling framework designed for the analysis of complex dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent uncertainty associated with these systems, limiting the ability to accurately represent evolution and understand system behavior. Our framework leverages Bayesian inference directly within the geometric modeling process, offering a more robust and mathematically rigorous approach. We present a comprehensive theoretical foundation and a practical implementation demonstrating significant improvements in system stability and uncertainty quantification compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around representing system evolution as a probabilistic mapping within a geometric framework, enabling precise quantification of uncertainty.

title: Foundations and Frontiers of Swahili Natural Language Processing
abstract: Swahili serves as a lingua franca for over 200 million speakers across East and Central Africa, functioning as a critical engine for digital societal interaction and economic integration. Despite its extensive demographic prominence, it remains acutely under-resourced within the computational domain of Natural Language Processing (NLP). This article presents a mathematically rigorous, systematic review of the Swahili NLP landscape, charting its historical trajectory from acute data scarcity to an emerging ecosystem of statistically specialised tools and representations. We comprehensively catalogue and mathematically categorise primary labelled datasets deployed for classification and generative tasks, including sentiment analysis, automatic speech recognition (ASR), and abstractive summarisation. Furthermore, we analyse the parameter optimisation, tokenisation dynamics, and architectural efficacy of dedicated foundational language models—such as SwahBERT, AfriBERTa, and specialised Large Language Models (LLMs)—mapping their performance bounds against Swahili’s highly agglutinative morphology. Beyond a mere structural inventory, this review critically exposes the “resource quality gap”, identifying profound statistical deficiencies in domain-specific corpora across high-stakes fields such as healthcare and law, whilst highlighting an acute lack of dialectal variance and fine-grained annotation schemes. The analysis concludes that while generalised parameter spaces have expanded, the absence of unified benchmarking infrastructures impedes systematic algorithmic validation. Finally, we propose actionable, statistically sound methodologies for future research, advocating for the collaborative construction of comprehensive multi-task benchmarks to bridge the digital divide for the Swahili-speaking populace.

title: Hybrid Architecture of Intelligent Systems with a Deterministic Core: from Concept to Prototype
abstract: The rapid development of large language models and autonomous intelligent agents has significantly expanded the capabilities of natural language processing and decision support. However, practical implementation reveals fundamental limitations, particularly in tasks requiring computational robustness, reproducibility of results, and strict information consistency. These issues are particularly critical in fields such as engineering, geometry, and educational systems, where plausible but inaccurate responses ("hallucinations") and unstable behavior undermine system trust. This paper proposes a hybrid intelligent architecture with a deterministic core to address these challenges. Unlike fully autonomous systems, the proposed approach decouples functions: an adaptive agent handles user interaction and its interpretation, while a stationary deterministic core provides robust computation, logical consistency, and graphical display. The architecture introduces a clear distinction between the development phase, which allows for iterative improvement, and the operational phase, characterized by a fixed core that guarantees reproducible and verifiable results. By providing protocol-based interaction between the agent and the deterministic core, the system ensures that all generated output—text, computational, and graphical—remains consistent and adheres to the underlying domain model. This hybrid structure combines the flexibility of modern intelligent agents with the precision and reliability of formal deterministic models, offering a robust foundation for mission-critical intelligent applications.

title: KI im Projektmanagement: Wie Peer-Groups den KI-Einstieg erleichtern
abstract: Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) ist für viele Unternehmen strategisch gesetzt – doch der Weg in konkrete Projekte bleibt oft unklar. Gerade im Mittelstand fehlt es an Orientierung und klaren Ansätzen, wie sich sinnvolle Anwendungsfälle identifizieren und priorisieren lassen. Der Beitrag zeigt am Beispiel einer unternehmensübergreifenden Peer-Group in Kassel, wie gemeinsames Lernen helfen kann, Unsicherheit zu reduzieren und KI-Initiativen schrittweise in das Projekt- und Multiprojektmanagement zu überführen. Durch kollegiale Beratung, Co-Creation-Workshops, Impulsvorträge und Unternehmensbesuche entwickeln sie ein praktisches Verständnis für KI-Vorhaben. Das Ergebnis: Mehr Orientierung, verbesserte Projektpriorisierung, verkürzte Lernzyklen, mehr Mut zum Experimentieren. Aus dem Austausch entstehen konkrete Projekte – teils unternehmensübergreifend.

title: The convergent laboratory: when AI reasoning, autonomous experiments, high performance and quantum computing reshape chemistry
abstract: This Comment emerges from TPC26 (https://tpc26.org), a conference convening leaders from academia, national laboratories, and industry who are reshaping materials science discovery. The meeting explored how AI, autonomous agents, self-driving labs, higher performance and quantum computing converge to amplify their individual impact on materials science discovery. The perspectives here reflect the firsthand experiences of researchers at these frontiers and capture the essence of this global endeavor. As AI-driven reasoning, autonomous agentic frameworks, self-driving laboratories, and fault-tolerant quantum processors mature simultaneously, we offer this Comment as a reference at what we believe is a tipping point of transformative advances and productive disruption in the chemical sciences.

title: Measuring the Novelty of Biomedical Papers Using the Latent Distances between Knowledge Units
abstract: Measuring the novelty of scientific papers is a central concern in research evaluation and scientometrics. From a recombination perspective, prior studies have largely focused on the co-occurrence of knowledge units to assess the novelty of scientific papers. However, these studies often overlook other relationships between knowledge units. This narrow view may result in inaccurate or incomplete evaluations of novelty for scientific papers. To fill this gap, this study introduces a comprehensive novelty measurement that incorporates three types of relationships between knowledge units: network, semantic, and hierarchical. These relationships are used to quantify the latent distances among knowledge units. Using a dataset of 142,036 articles published in PLoS ONE and a validation dataset from the H1 Connect platform, our results demonstrate that (1) each relationship type captures distinct latent distances between MeSH terms; (2) compared to the widely used indicators proposed by Uzzi et al. (2013), our measures show stronger alignment with peer judgements; and (3) combining all three distance metrics yields more effective identification of novel papers than using any single perspective alone.

title: RefactorPlatform: An Open-Source Harness for Controlled Evaluation of Repository-Scale Refactoring Agents
abstract: Repository-scale refactoring requires coding agents to propagate a single change across many interdependent files without altering program behavior, yet to our knowledge no existing harness isolates the design choices that determine agent success on this task. We present RefactorPlatform, an open-source evaluation harness that holds the environment fixed and varies each design axis explicitly: model backbone (via OpenRouter and GitHub Copilot CLI), execution regime (baseline, retrieval-augmented, and multi-agent), and prompt specificity. Each run executes in an isolated workspace with live terminal streaming, per-task logging of tokens, diffs, and transcripts, AST-based verification, and exportable telemetry for audit and reproduction. Demonstrating the platform on 100 multi-file RefactorBench tasks across four model families, we illustrate the analyses it supports: AST-aware chunking outperforms naive token-window chunking by 25-30 percentage points (pp) across prompt modes, whereas naive retrieval falls below the retrieval-free baseline; a lean retrieval-augmented single agent (86%) beats the sub-agent configuration we evaluated (66%) on matched tasks with no task passing under delegation that fails under retrieval; and retrieval's accuracy gains absorb its token overhead, leaving cost per successful refactoring unchanged. RefactorPlatform is open-sourced to make refactoring-agent evaluation reproducible and auditable.

title: The Cross-Correlation Distribution of the Niho-Type Decimation $d=4(2^m-1)+1$
abstract: The cross-correlation problem is a classical problem in sequence design. In this paper, we determine the cross-correlation distribution of the Niho-type decimation $d=4(2^m-1)+1$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$ for every positive integer $m$. With $q=2^m$, this is equivalent to determining the distribution of the number of roots in $U_{q+1}$ of $f_a(x)=x^7+ax^4+\bar a x^3+1$ for $a\in\mathbb F_{q^2}$, where $U_{q+1}=\{x\in\mathbb F_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\}$. The main difficulty is to count the four-element subsets of $U_{q+1}$ that may occur as root sets of $f_a$. We normalize such subsets by their product and study the resulting condition through the associated resolvent. This reduces the required enumeration to several equations over $\mathbb F_q$, which are evaluated by character sums and Kloosterman sums. The remaining mixed Kloosterman sum is related to a Kloosterman sum over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$ and is evaluated using a theorem of Carlitz. Consequently, we obtain explicit formulas for all the frequencies in the cross-correlation distribution.

title: Spin Teleportation via Bell-Triplet States Emergent from Proton-Proton Scattering
abstract: Entanglement is a key resource in quantum information science, yet its properties and applications in nuclear systems remain largely unexplored. Here, using proton-proton scattering as a quantum laboratory, we report the emergence of a near-pure Bell-triplet state at a laboratory energy of 151 MeV and a center-of-mass scattering angle of 90°. In this unique kinematic regime, the scattering amplitude functions as a transition operator connecting distinct Bell states. Building upon this emergent resource, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for proton spins, exploiting the intrinsic Hamiltonian of the strong interaction to perform the requisite Bell measurement effectively. These findings effectively bridge few-body nuclear physics and quantum technology, establishing proton-proton scattering as both a source of high-fidelity entanglement and a natural processor for quantum information.

title: NeSy-RegReason: A Neuro-Symbolic AI Framework for Interpretable and Adaptive Regulatory Compliance in Financial Services
abstract: Financial compliance systems must identify suspicious behaviour while also showing which legal obligations, facts, and exceptions support each decision. Purely neural models learn complex transaction patterns but usually provide post-hoc explanations that do not constitute legal reasoning; conventional rule engines are inspectable but brittle under behavioural and regulatory change. This study presents NeSy-RegReason, a neuro-symbolic framework combining Transformer and graph neural prediction, a versioned regulatory knowledge graph, OWL/SWRL/Prolog inference, rule-conflict resolution, counterfactual explanation, and an immutable audit trace. Evaluation uses author-supplied results across IEEE-CIS, PaySim, Elliptic, and a 500,000-record synthetic multi-regulation dataset. NeSy-RegReason attained 95.86% accuracy, 0.956 F1-score, 0.986 ROC-AUC, and 0.918 Matthews correlation coefficient. It achieved 98.31% compliance detection with 1.89% false positives, 0.97 explanation fidelity, 99.12% audit-trace completeness, and 98.54% conflict resolution. Wilcoxon comparisons against five principal baselines were significant (p ≤ .002; effect sizes 0.68–0.83). Ablation results show that symbolic reasoning is the most consequential component for explainability and auditability. The findings indicate that compliance performance should be evaluated as a multi-objective problem spanning prediction, rule satisfaction, explanation fidelity, trace reproducibility, and adaptation latency. Because the supplied aggregate results do not include run-level observations, code, or an external replication package, the statistical claims are reported as supplied and require independent reproduction before operational deployment.

title: Classification of Selected Author Styles in Post-Millennium World Literature Based on Stylometric Characteristics
abstract: Bu çalışma, milenyum sonrası dünya edebiyatında öne çıkan yazarların üsluplarını hesaplamalı stilometri, doğal dil işleme ve makine öğrenmesi yöntemleriyle incelemektedir. Çalışma kapsamında J. M. Coetzee, Orhan Pamuk, Herta Müller, Mario Vargas Llosa, Mo Yan, Alice Munro, Kazuo Ishiguro, Olga Tokarczuk, Abdulrazak Gurnah, Annie Ernaux, Jon Fosse, Han Kang ve László Krasznahorkai’nin seçili eserlerinden oluşan çok kültürlü bir edebi korpus oluşturulmuştur. Metinler ön işleme süreçlerinden geçirilmiş, yaklaşık 1000 kelimelik segmentlere ayrılmış ve sözcüksel, biçimsel, sözdizimsel ve n-gram tabanlı stilometrik özellikler çıkarılmıştır. Elde edilen özellikler Linear SVM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest ve Logistic Regression gibi makine öğrenmesi modelleriyle değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, özellikle Word TF-IDF özellikleriyle eğitilen Linear SVM modelinin yüksek sınıflandırma başarısı gösterdiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışma, yazar üslubunun hesaplamalı yöntemlerle modellenebilen çok katmanlı bir yapı olduğunu göstermekte; aynı zamanda dijital beşeri bilimler ve kültürlerarası edebiyat araştırmaları için yeni bir analitik çerçeve sunmaktadır.

Metinler ön işleme süreçlerinden geçirilmiş, yaklaşık 1000 kelimelik segmentlere ayrılmış ve sözcüksel, biçimsel, sözdizimsel ve n-gram tabanlı stilometrik özellikler çıkarılmıştır. Elde edilen özellikler Linear SVM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest ve Logistic Regression gibi makine öğrenmesi modelleriyle değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, özellikle Word TF-IDF özellikleriyle eğitilen Linear SVM modelinin yüksek sınıflandırma başarısı gösterdiğini ortaya koymaktadır. title: Quantum State-Driven Machine Learning Auto-Selection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning, termed Quantum State-Driven Machine Learning Auto-Selection, which leverages the unique properties of quantum states to automate the selection of optimal features and model parameters. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting model parameters based on the quantum state, allowing the algorithm to explore the parameter space more efficiently and discover superior model configurations. Traditional machine learning relies heavily on human-defined parameters, while this approach seeks to automate this process through the inherent properties of quantum mechanics. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum mechanics principles used, and its potential impact on model performance through a detailed analysis. We provide a comprehensive overview of the proposed method, including mathematical formulations and illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness. The study explores the potential of this approach to address limitations of conventional machine learning algorithms.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Neural Networks (ASNN) Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates and develops an adaptive self-organizing neural network (ASNN) structure optimization algorithm. The core goal is to enhance neural network performance by dynamically adjusting network node connection weights. We introduce a novel mechanism that allows for continuous, real-time weight adjustment during training, leading to improved efficiency and potentially better model generalization. The proposed algorithm focuses on a feedback loop between the network's output and the adjustment of weights, enabling the network to adapt to changing data patterns. This approach contrasts with traditional static optimization techniques, offering a more responsive and potentially superior solution for neural network design. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, analyzes its performance through simulations and a limited experimental setup, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Networks
abstract: Quantum topology networks (QTN) represent a promising paradigm for quantum information processing and communication, leveraging the unique properties of quantum geometry to enable enhanced data transmission and manipulation. This paper explores the design and implementation of an adaptive quantum topology network, which dynamically adjusts network topology to optimize quantum information flow and significantly enhance quantum communication capabilities. We present a novel approach utilizing a feedback loop to continuously refine the network's structure, improving the robustness and efficiency of quantum data transfer. The core mechanism involves adjusting node positions, edge weights, and even the topology itself, all guided by a dynamic optimization algorithm. The advantages of this approach – dynamic adaptability, improved communication efficiency, and enhanced robustness – are discussed, highlighting its potential impact on the field of quantum computing.

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction from E8 Root Lattice Self-Duality — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 E8 root vectors form a self-dual even lattice whose packing geometry naturally encodes a topological quantum error-correcting code, where the 132Hz base frequency establishes the energy gap protecting logical qubits from decoherence. The Tutte polynomial specialization over finite fields classifies error syndrome configurations by mapping combinatorial hyperplane arrangements to lattice defect structures, while the φ^k frequency scaling of modular phase-space coordinates defines the logical encoding manifold. This unifies the phase interference dynamics of quantum tunneling, the combinatorial algebra of characteristic polynomials, and the entanglement-preserving pathways into a single geometric framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Continuous Learning Model (QCLM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Continuous Learning Model (QCLM) leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to address the challenges inherent in continuous learning scenarios involving multiple, interconnected quantum data sources. The core idea is to establish an entanglement network between these data sources, allowing for the extraction of information and the continuous, high-precision modeling of the overall system state. Unlike traditional machine learning approaches that rely on classical data and discrete training steps, QCLM exploits the non-classical nature of quantum entanglement to facilitate information fusion across data sources and achieve superior performance, particularly in high-dimensional, non-linear, and highly correlated quantum datasets. The model continuously updates its quantum state representation and utilizes the entanglement network for dynamic information integration, resulting in robust and adaptive learning capabilities. Mathematical formulations detail the key components of the QCLM, including the entanglement network structure, the quantum state representation, and the update rules governing the learning process. This approach offers a promising pathway for developing advanced quantum learning systems capable of handling complex, dynamic environments. ---
