title: Quantum Adaptive Simulation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Simulation Algorithm (QASA) presents a novel approach to quantum simulation, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance the fidelity and accuracy of simulations. This research focuses on designing an adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts simulation parameters based on the quantum state of the system being modeled, optimizing the simulation process for improved results. We explore the potential of QASA to overcome limitations of existing classical simulation methods, particularly in simulating complex systems with intricate dynamics. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate system states, leading to a more precise and efficient simulation compared to traditional techniques. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting its potential impact on various scientific disciplines.

title: ##基于深度学习的符号推理自动生成
abstract: This paper explores the development of a deep learning-based system for automated symbolic reasoning generation. Traditional symbolic reasoning relies heavily on human expertise in defining and maintaining rules, a process that is both time-consuming and prone to errors. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing deep learning models to learn the underlying rules and patterns inherent in symbolic reasoning processes, thereby automating the generation of these rules. We investigate the application of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and Transformer architectures to capture the nuances of symbolic reasoning, focusing on the representation and relationships of information within these processes. The ultimate goal is to create a more efficient and reliable system for reasoning, particularly in domains where manual rule definition is a significant bottleneck. The core of this work lies in leveraging the ability of deep learning models to learn from data without explicit programming, offering a potentially transformative shift in how we approach symbolic reasoning. This paper details the proposed architecture, explores potential applications, and discusses future research directions. ---

title: Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network learning, termed Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Learning (ANDTL). The core claim is that the topology of neuronal connections can adapt dynamically to task requirements, thereby enhancing both learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. The proposed mechanism utilizes a reinforcement learning-based algorithm to optimize the topology and connection weights within a neural network. Unlike traditional methods focused solely on adjusting weights, ANDTL introduces a dynamic adjustment of both structural and weight parameters. The system learns to rewire connections and even add or remove neurons based on the feedback received from a reward function, allowing it to converge to a more efficient and effective topology for a given task. This approach addresses limitations of conventional neural networks, particularly in scenarios with complex and evolving data distributions, where a fixed topology may not be optimal. The theoretical underpinnings of ANDTL are explored, and the potential benefits of this dynamic topology learning are discussed. The paper concludes with a high-level overview of the algorithm and its potential applications. ---

title: Quantum Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum adaptive topology transformations to revolutionize quantum state conversion, particularly within the realms of quantum computing and quantum key distribution. Traditional quantum state conversion methods often rely on classical transformations, presenting limitations in efficiency and scalability. This research introduces a novel algorithm leveraging quantum topology transformations to dynamically adjust quantum states, thereby significantly enhancing the speed and efficacy of state conversion processes. The core mechanism focuses on systematically manipulating the quantum state through topology-based operations to achieve optimal transformations. We detail the algorithm's design, including the mathematical formulation of the topology transformations and their impact on state evolution. The significance of this approach lies in its potential to overcome limitations inherent in classical approaches, offering a pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum operations.

abstract: การสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตมีความสําคัญในภาคธุรกิจ เนื่องจากองค์กรจําเป็นต้องตอบสนองต่อเหตุการณ์ที่อาจกระทบต่อชื่อเสียง ความเชื่อมั่น และพฤติกรรมของผู้มีส่วนได้ส่วนเสียอย่างรวดเร็วและรอบคอบ ขณะเดียวกัน โมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่มีศักยภาพในการช่วยร่างข้อความหรือคําแถลงที่มีความสอดคล้องกับบริบทของภาษา แต่การนํามาใช้ในงานสื่อสารต่อสาธารณะยังต้องพิจารณาอย่างระมัดระวัง เนื่องจากข้อความที่สร้างโดยปัญญาประดิษฐ์อาจมีความเสี่ยงด้านความคลาดเคลื่อนของข้อเท็จจริง หรือไม่สอดคล้องกับบริบทและวัตถุประสงค์ของการสื่อสาร ดังนั้นการเลือกที่เหมาะสมจึงไม่สามารถพิจารณาเพียงการร่างคําแถลงเท่านั้น แต่ต้องประเมินคุณภาพของข้อความในมิติต่างๆ ที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตด้วยงานวิจัยนี้มุ่งศึกษาการสร้าง การประเมิน และการตัดสินร่างคําแถลงจากข่าวสถานการณ์วิกฤตของบริษัทเอกชนในประเทศไทย โดยใช้กรอบทฤษฎีการสื่อสารที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตเป็นแนวทางในการสร้างและประเมินข้อความ และนําผลลัพธ์ที่ได้จากโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่หลายโมเดลมาประเมินและตัดสินกันด้วยแนวทาง LLM-as-a-Judge เพื่อใช้ในการสนับสนุนการตัดสินใจว่าโมเดลใดสามารถร่างคําแถลงที่มีคุณภาพและเหมาะสมกับบริบทการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตทางธุรกิจในภาษาไทยมากที่สุด นอกจากนี้ งานวิจัยยังเปรียบเทียบผลการตัดสินของ LLM-as-a-Judge กับผลการประเมินจากมนุษย์ เพื่อพิจารณาระดับความสอดคล้องระหว่างการตัดสินของปัญญาประดิษฐ์กับการตัดสินของมนุษย์ในงานด้านการสื่อสารผลที่คาดว่าจะได้รับจากงานวิจัยนี้ คือแนวทางเชิงปฏิบัติสําหรับการประเมินและคัดเลือกโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่ที่เหมาะสมต่อการร่างคําแถลงเพื่อการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตทางธุรกิจในภาษาไทย รวมถึงความเข้าใจเกี่ยวกับศักยภาพและข้อจํากัดของการใช้ LLM-as-a-Judge ในการประเมินงานด้านการสื่อสารแบบปลายเปิด

title: Continual Graph Memory for Adaptive Recommendation under Intent Drift
abstract: This paper studies adaptive recommendation under intent drift, where feedback from each recommendation outcome can reveal whether the relational evidence used for ranking is useful, missing, or misleading. While Knowledge Graphs (KGs) provide essential semantic structure to handle these shifts, traditional KG-enhanced systems treat the graph as a static retrieval substrate, making it brittle to evolving intents, noisy metadata, and recurring failure patterns. This paper proposes CGM-Rec, a continual graph memory framework for adaptive recommendation. CGM-Rec treats the graph state as a writable memory and maintains two complementary components. Therein, a Semantic Graph Memory is updated conservatively through quality-gated typed operations for storing stable and high-confidence relational knowledge. Meanwhile, an Episodic Lesson Memory acts as a fast reactive memory that learns recent outcomes, failure cases, and corrective hints. During testing, model parameters remain frozen and adaptation occurs only through memory writes. We evaluate CGM-Rec under a frozen-parameter, one-pass reranking protocol, where encoders and prompts remain fixed during testing and adaptation occurs only through memory writes. Experiments across multiple recommendation settings show that CGM-Rec improves over evaluated neural and LLM-based baselines on most metrics. Particularly, under sampled-candidate reranking, CGM-Rec improves HR@1 by up to 29.58% over the strongest LLM baseline on Bundle, and outperforms K-RagRec on metadata-rich ML-100K with HR@5 of 0.5941 versus 0.4746.

title: NEXUS X AUTONOMOUS INTELLIGENCE AND ACTION PLATFORM
authors: 1Yamini Chouhan, 2 Baler Simon , 3 G Prashanth Kumar, 4 M Anjali, 5 B S Mahalakshmi
abstract: NEXUS X – Autonomous Intelligence and Action Platform is an intelligent software platform designed to go beyond traditional systems that only provide information or respond to user commands. The platform combines Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and automation technologies to understand user requirements, analyze information, make decisions, and perform appropriate actions with minimal human intervention. The proposed platform acts as an intelligent assistant that can receive user goals or tasks, understand their intent, break complex requirements into smaller steps, and determine suitable actions. It can analyze available data, generate recommendations, execute predefined workflows, monitor task progress, and provide results to the user. The system can also maintain context from previous interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of its responses and actions. The main objective of NEXUS X is to create a unified autonomous platform that can transform user instructions into meaningful and actionable outcomes. Instead of requiring users to manually perform every step, the system can automate repetitive tasks, support decision-making, manage workflows, and provide intelligent recommendations. This can improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and enable faster completion of complex tasks. Overall, NEXUS X – Autonomous Intelligence and Action Platform provides a foundation for developing intelligent, goal-oriented applications capable of reasoning and taking controlled actions. The platform can be further enhanced with AI agents, real-time data integration, multi-agent collaboration, voice interaction, predictive analytics, personalized automation, external API integration, and advanced security and authorization mechanisms.

title: Feedback-free photonic reservoir computing based on multimode temporal coding in semiconductor ring lasers
abstract: 半导体环形激光器 (SRL) 天然支持顺时针与逆时针两个反向传播模式, 是构建光子神经形态计算的重要器件。然而, 基于 SRL 的光子储备池计算大多依赖物理反馈环来提供衰落记忆, 存在参数整定困难、稳定区间有限等问题。本文将单个 SRL 与受生物启发的准卷积 (QC) 编码相结合, 提出一种无反馈光子储备池计算方案, 依据 QC 编码施加位置的不同, 构建了输入编码型 (IC-RC)、输出编码型 (OC-RC) 与混合编码型 (HC-RC) 三种互补储备池变体, 三者分别通过在输入端、输出端或两端同时施加编码来提供差异化的算法记忆。通过建立速率方程模型, 在混沌时间序列预测、非线性信道均衡与线性记忆容量三项基准任务上, 分析了注入强度、频率失谐以及 QC核关键参数对三种方案性能的影响。结果表明, 三种方案均明显优于传统时延储备池计算。本文还发现不同的编码方案具有不同的优势, 其中 IC-RC 预测性能最优, HC-RC 记忆保持能力最强,输出层激活函数可进一步改善预测与信道均衡性能, 而对记忆容量影响甚微。本文结果不仅验证了所提方案的有效性, 也为构建高度可集成的光子神经形态计算系统提供了新的思路。

title: Multimedia Integration and Cultural Heritage Innovation Pathways in Traditional Pipa Performance Teaching in the Digital Age
abstract: This paper will investigate how the pipa can integrate multimedia technologies within its teaching practices for overcoming major teaching challenges such as teacher shortages, standardized teaching, and inadequate support for individual differences among students. The proposed model will include intelligent diagnostic systems using audio analysis for performance assessment and learning path recommendations, multi-media teaching aids with digitized scores and multi-angle teaching videos, as well as teaching plans based on individual students’ levels of proficiency. Design for cultural heritage content will focus on digital recreation of historical settings, multi-media interpretation for regional teaching characteristics, as well as developing aesthetic competency with links to traditional art values. Implementation assistance will include upgrading teachers’ digital literacy skills, improving evaluation systems with technical-humanistic dimensions, as well as developing institutional sharing platforms for teaching resources. This comprehensive teaching platform views multimedia technology as an enabler that complements existing pipa pedagogy while maintaining cultural authenticity, contributing a pipa-calibrated integration model, a cultural heritage innovation pathway, and implementation mechanisms that extend master-apprentice transmission through digital means.

title: Axiomatizing Atomic Numbers in ChEBI
abstract: This post describes how I produced a novel ontology module that axiomatizes the atomic numbers for ChEBI terms representing atoms (i.e., subclasses of CHEBI:33250) using subclass expressions with data restrictions, and the ROBOT template magic that made it possible.

title: Continuity Kernel: A Cognitive Architecture and AI Safety Framework for Persistent Artificial Identity
abstract: Continuity Kernel / CK-01 is a computational cognitive architecture and AI safety framework for persistent artificial identity. This v1.0.0 record includes the full manuscript, editable source, a one-command synthetic benchmark, exact configurations and seeds, raw machine-readable results, manifests, SHA-256 hashes, tests, gate specifications, and legacy evidence bundles. The claims are limited to architecture design and synthetic validation; the work does not claim empirical validation of consciousness, human cognition, or real-world autonomous-agent safety.

title: Native Cognition Kernel (NCK) 0.1
abstract: Native Cognition Kernel (NCK) 0.1 is a mathematically specified architecture for deterministic, bounded, provenance-aware machine cognition. NCK defines cognition as an explicit system of typed symbolic state, proof-governed inference, hypothesis formation, prediction, falsification, revision, planning, action, and adaptation under changing rules and environments.Rather than defining cognitive behavior through a trained statistical model, NCK specifies its cognitive operations directly as finite mathematical objects, relations, operators, invariants, and certified state transitions. The architecture is designed so that its semantics are independent of any particular software implementation, programming language, execution platform, or hardware realization.This release contains the authoritative NCK 0.1 Normative Mathematical Specification, its typeset publication, and the Executable Logic companion, which develops the formal system through explicit paper-executable examples. The Markdown mathematical specification is the sole normative mathematical authority for NCK 0.1; the accompanying publications are subordinate to that specification.The architecture is intended to support direct implementation and formal verification, including software proof-of-concept implementations and, where developed and separately validated, formal-proof and digital-hardware realizations such as Lean, Verilog, or VHDL representations.The release includes an external SHA-256 manifest identifying the exact immutable artifacts constituting NCK 0.1. NCK defines cognition as an explicit system of typed symbolic state, proof-governed inference, hypothesis formation, prediction, falsification, revision, planning, action, and adaptation under changing rules and environments.Rather than defining cognitive behavior through a trained statistical model, NCK specifies its cognitive operations directly as finite mathematical objects, relations, operators, invariants, and certified state transitions. The architecture is designed so that its semantics are independent of any particular software implementation, programming language, execution platform, or hardware realization.This release contains the authoritative NCK 0.1 Normative Mathematical Specification, its typeset publication, and the Executable Logic companion, which develops the formal system through explicit paper-executable examples. The Markdown mathematical specification is the sole normative mathematical authority for NCK 0.1; the accompanying publications are subordinate to that specification.The architecture is intended to support direct implementation and formal verification, including software proof-of-concept implementations and, where developed and separately validated, formal-proof and digital-hardware realizations such as Lean, Verilog, or VHDL representations.The release includes an external SHA-256 manifest identifying the exact immutable artifacts constituting NCK 0.1. title: Title: Adaptive Chaos for Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive chaos to enhance deep learning architectures, aiming to improve both performance and stability during training. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the structure of the network – specifically, layer sizes, connection strengths, and activation function parameters – based on real-time monitoring of training progress. This self-tuning chaos mechanism, driven by a feedback loop, allows the network to evolve and optimize itself, potentially exceeding the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. The core idea is to mimic the inherent dynamics of chaotic systems, leveraging a carefully crafted 'chaos' component to guide the learning process. The integration of chaos into a core deep learning technique offers a promising path toward more robust and efficient deep learning models. This work presents a preliminary framework and demonstrates its potential through a simplified implementation of a neural network with adaptive chaos.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的自组织机器学习 (ASML)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing machine learning framework, termed ASML, based on adaptive topology. Traditional machine learning models often struggle to accurately represent and model complex system behaviors, and ASML offers a new toolset for this purpose. The core of ASML lies in the implementation of an adaptive topology structure, which allows the model to dynamically adjust its representation to better capture the intricacies of the data. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples, focusing on a system exhibiting self-organized patterns. The paper elucidates the mechanism behind ASML and its potential impact on machine learning research.

title: 基于自适应的量子模拟的容错优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Simulation with Error Mitigation," designed to address the challenges of quantum simulation, particularly concerning error mitigation. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameter adjustments, leading to inherent stochasticity and potential inaccuracies. This work proposes a self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy, leveraging quantum system dynamics to dynamically refine simulation parameters, thereby significantly reducing random errors during the simulation process. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a continuous assessment and adjustment of key simulation variables, resulting in improved accuracy and reliability of quantum simulations. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, provides a rigorous analysis of its performance, and explores its potential for enhancing the quality of quantum computations. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to mitigate errors in a specific quantum system simulation scenario. The study concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this approach.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应几何优化
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric optimization. Traditional geometric optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, high-dimensional shapes due to computational limitations. We propose a novel algorithm, Quantum Geometry Optimizer (QGO), that utilizes entangled quantum states to represent and manipulate geometric configurations, offering a potential pathway to significantly enhance optimization efficiency and handle intricate shapes. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the unique properties of entanglement to create a dynamic and adaptive optimization process. This work provides a theoretical foundation and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this approach. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications of this technology for various fields.

title: Quantum Entanglement Beyond Symmetry: Towards Enhanced Computational Capabilities
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. However, the inherent fragility of entangled states poses significant challenges to building practical and scalable quantum computers. This paper explores the concept of quantum entanglement's non-symmetry, proposing a novel approach – the incorporation of non-symmetry into quantum computations – to enhance stability and unlock new computational capabilities. We investigate how this approach mitigates the limitations of single-state entanglement and paves the way for fundamentally different algorithms. The core claim is that strategically introducing non-symmetry into quantum algorithms can lead to improved resilience and performance, offering a pathway to more robust and capable quantum systems. This work details a mechanism for encoding and manipulating non-symmetric entangled states, illustrating its potential impact on quantum computation. We present a preliminary analysis of this approach and outline future research directions, emphasizing the importance of understanding and harnessing the power of non-symmetry in quantum information processing.

title: Nonlinear Time Series Systems and Deep Reinforcement Learning Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the fusion of nonlinear time series systems (NTS) modeling with reinforcement learning (RL) for addressing complex control problems characterized by high nonlinearity and time-varying dynamics. The core idea is to leverage the representation power of NTS models to capture system behavior and then utilize RL algorithms for policy optimization. Deep learning techniques are integrated for feature extraction and representation learning, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional RL methods in handling intricate nonlinear systems. The proposed approach offers a novel way to tackle control problems where explicit system models are difficult to obtain, relying instead on learning from data. The research demonstrates the potential of this combined approach to achieve robust and adaptive control performance.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Collaborative Optimization of Non-Classical Computing Resources
abstract: This research investigates a novel approach to quantum algorithm design and resource allocation by synergistically combining quantum error correction (QEC) coding with the characteristics of non-classical computing resources, such as quantum heat reservoirs and quantum noise. The core premise is that traditional optimization strategies for QEC and non-classical resource utilization operate independently, neglecting the potential for mutual benefit. We propose a framework centered around probabilistic quantum algorithm optimizers that simulate algorithm performance under varying resource conditions. These optimizers dynamically adjust both quantum algorithm parameters and QEC schemes based on the simulated performance, aiming to achieve significantly improved efficiency. This work addresses a critical gap in the field by moving beyond isolated optimization efforts and establishing a fundamental connection between the robustness of QEC and the practical limitations imposed by non-classical computing environments. The methodology leverages advanced probabilistic modeling and optimization techniques to provide a robust and adaptive approach to quantum algorithm design.

title: 基于动态量子纠缠的拓扑几何验证
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum geometry validation utilizing dynamic quantum entanglement. We propose a method that leverages the inherent properties of entangled quantum states to simulate and verify complex topological structures with unprecedented precision. Traditional topological calculations often struggle with approximation errors and require significant computational resources. This research introduces a dynamically-generated quantum state model, employing entanglement to mimic the evolution of topological phenomena, and utilizing quantum effects to precisely characterize their properties. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a robust, accurate, and accelerated computational framework for topological analysis. This work represents a significant advancement, demonstrating the potential for a fundamentally new approach to topological computation, surpassing current limitations through enhanced precision and computational efficiency.

title: Quantum Topological Chaos Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topological Chaos Optimization (QTCO) presents a novel algorithmic approach to optimization, leveraging the principles of quantum topicity chaos – a theoretical framework that describes complex systems exhibiting unique, non-linear, and highly sensitive behavior. This research focuses on developing a self-adaptive optimization algorithm predicated on this chaotic structure, aiming to improve the stability and robustness of complex systems. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement and topological structure to dynamically adjust system parameters and propagate solutions, thereby achieving enhanced performance. This paper outlines the design of QTCO, detailing its core concepts, methodology, and preliminary results demonstrating its potential for optimizing challenging systems.

title: 异质性感知学习的自适应感知算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive perception algorithm based on the principle of '异质性感知' – dynamically adjusting perceptual thresholds and model parameters to effectively model and identify complex data distributions. Traditional perception algorithms typically rely on fixed thresholds, while this approach leverages the inherent heterogeneity of data to dynamically adjust perception, enhancing model capabilities for complex datasets. We present a framework for implementing this dynamic adjustment using a novel weighting mechanism. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a series of quantitative evaluations on several benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance in identifying intricate patterns and reducing classification errors compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The core mechanism focuses on continuous parameter adjustment based on data distribution characteristics, offering a robust and adaptable solution for diverse perception tasks.

title: Self-Adapting Quantum State Prediction and Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive quantum state prediction as a novel approach to algorithm optimization within the quantum computing realm. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on computationally expensive pre-calculations, limiting their practical efficiency. We propose a new algorithmic framework leveraging self-adaptive quantum state prediction to dynamically adjust quantum operations, thereby significantly enhancing algorithm performance. This research explores the design of a system that predicts the state of a quantum system and uses this prediction to intelligently guide the execution of quantum circuits. The core mechanism centers around real-time state evolution and optimization, resulting in improved efficiency. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the benefits and challenges associated with this approach and outlines a roadmap for future advancements in quantum algorithm design.

title: Adaptive Quantum Interference Optimization of Spacetime
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum interference optimization to enhance the performance of complex systems, specifically focusing on optimizing algorithm efficiency and computational precision. The core concept centers around leveraging the unique properties of quantum interference – a phenomenon where quantum systems can constructively or destructively interfere – to dynamically adjust system parameters and improve computational results. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, while this work proposes a novel approach utilizing this interference to achieve more effective and adaptable optimization. The research explores the potential of this method to address challenges in various fields, including machine learning and computational modeling, by providing a framework for robust and efficient optimization. The paper details the methodology, presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and concludes with future directions for research and development.

title: Waveform-driven prediction of transmon qubit energy spectra using a physics-informed path-transformed transformer trained on Josephson junction dynamics.
abstract: Extracting the energy spectrum of a superconducting transmon qubit requires time-consuming microwave spectroscopy that must be repeated following every thermal cycle or parameter drift event. We introduce the Physics-Informed Path-Transformed (PaTH) Transformer, a surrogate model trained exclusively on resistively-shunted Josephson junction (RCSJ) numerical simulations, which predicts the five lowest energy eigenvalues and the anharmonicity from a raw DC voltage waveform. The model is trained on 10,000 simulated circuits spanning the realistic transmon parameter space (EJ /EC ∈ [10.7, 300], f01/h ∈ [2.6, 13.3] GHz) and evaluated on 1,500 independent test circuits, achieving mean absolute energy error 0.886 μeV (R2 ≥ 0.998 per level) and transition-frequency spacing error 2.14%, with GPU inference completing in 8.70 ms per circuit. A curriculum-ramped physics loss incorporating Josephson monotonicity, quantization spacing, anharmonicity sign, and Lindblad-Heisenberg constraints produces physically self-consistent predictions throughout training. Treating anharmonicity as a direct sixth output resolves a gradient-scale conflict (∼25× imbalance) that prevents reliable convergence when it is inferred post-hoc from level differences. The model delivers, from a single forward pass: DRAG gate fidelity ⟨F⟩ = 0.99982 at 3.9 ns; dispersive readout shift −14.3 MHz; macroscopic quantum tunneling crossover at 56.6 mK; SQUID tunable range 5.95 GHz; and inverse-design frequency errors below 0.05 kHz. Zero-noise extrapolation across five dilution-refrigerator temperatures confirms that model accuracy already reaches the Johnson-Nyquist noise floor, with the macroscopic quantum tunneling crossover temperature providing a physics-derived accuracy benchmark independent of model architecture. Validated against eight published experimental spectra from four independent laboratories, the surrogate achieves mean f01 error 1929 MHz versus 1935 MHz for exact Hamiltonian diagonalization, demonstrating that RCSJ waveform encoding conveys device-level physics that the static ideal Hamiltonian cannot represent.
